metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe-index verify <data-dir> --json`: the integrity check of one index data directory — file hashes recomputed against `repomd.json`, mismatches and missing files named, one honest `ok` verdict. Read by scripts and agents, CI above all (a failed check also exits non-zero — the JSON is what the pipeline logs; PROP-044 §6.5, `foreign_parsers = many`). Source of truth for the writer: `crates/vibe-index/src/cli/verify.rs` (`Report`, `Mismatch`); the generated reader this schema owns lives in `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index_cli/e1/verify_report/`.
The data directory as the ask spelled it — a `PathBuf` on the wire, verbatim: an absolute ask echoes absolute, a relative one relative.
The registry name the checked manifest announces, from `repomd.json`.
The manifest's package count, echoed from `repomd.json`.
The manifest's version count, echoed from `repomd.json`.
How many manifest entries were checked (files hashed, the `by-name` directory counted). Bounded by construction and checked at the wire boundary.
Every checked entry whose observed size or hash diverged from the manifest. Required member: a clean check writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no skip here.
Relative paths of manifest files that could not be read at all. Required member: a complete directory writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no skip here.
The verdict: `mismatches` and `missing` are both empty. The command's exit code follows this field (non-zero on `false`) — a script may read either, and they cannot disagree.

One checked entry whose observed bytes diverged from what `repomd.json` claims — a file hash/size mismatch, or a `by-name` directory whose entry count moved. The `directory` flavour of the check (a moved entry count) reports `"directory"` in both sha256 fields and the counts as the entry sizes.
The entry's path relative to the data directory, as the manifest keys it.

File size in bytes, encoded as a canonical decimal string - ASCII digits only, no sign, no leading zeros except the bare `0`, value within the unsigned 64-bit range. Integers wider than 32 bits ride the wire as decimal strings by the owner's standing rule (2026-08-20, PROP-044 `##M-WIDE-INTEGERS-AS-STRINGS`; first application `formats/breaks/003.md`): JTD has no 64-bit integer type, so the string form is the only way this schema can describe the writer's `u64` truthfully. A non-canonical string or a JSON number is refused loudly at value-parse time, never coerced. The size `repomd.json` records for this file.

File size in bytes, encoded as a canonical decimal string - ASCII digits only, no sign, no leading zeros except the bare `0`, value within the unsigned 64-bit range. Integers wider than 32 bits ride the wire as decimal strings by the owner's standing rule (2026-08-20, PROP-044 `##M-WIDE-INTEGERS-AS-STRINGS`; first application `formats/breaks/003.md`): JTD has no 64-bit integer type, so the string form is the only way this schema can describe the writer's `u64` truthfully. A non-canonical string or a JSON number is refused loudly at value-parse time, never coerced. The size the file actually has on disk.
The hash the manifest claims (`sha256:`-prefixed hex; the literal `"directory"` for the directory flavour of the check).
The hash the recomputed bytes produced (`sha256:`-prefixed hex; the literal `"directory"` for the directory flavour of the check).
